title: Marlin Installed Cockpit Provider Attestation v1

executable_digest.description: sha256 of executable_digest_target, the file that actually determines the provider behavior, verified by Cockpit both at registration and immediately before every spawn (post-registration file swaps are caught, not just install-time ones). Null or absent means the attestation predates this check and Cockpit will reject it until the provider is reinstalled. NOTE ON THREAT MODEL: this authenticates the executable against attestation.json, not against Marlin itself — signature is still null, so an actor able to overwrite the executable on disk can equally overwrite attestation.json with a matching digest. This detects accidental drift/corruption/partial installs, not a fully compromised local write path.

executable_digest_target.description: Absolute path of the file executable_digest was computed over. Must be an explicit choice by the attester (Marlin), never inferred positionally by Cockpit — e.g. installer.ts sets this to executable itself for a standalone binary like niji's, or to a provider script path for an interpreter+script runtime like marlin-dxp's own self-registration, where executable is the generic process.execPath Node runtime. Cockpit additionally requires this to equal executable or a declared entry in args, so the attestation cannot claim to verify a file unrelated to what is actually spawned.
